minor.issue: Describes the comparator as 'non-protein controls', but the pooled non-MIP group included protein-supplemented control conditions (source: 'five of the control conditions included a PRO supplemented group').
Moderate quality is attributed to inconsistency (heterogeneity), and TBM was rated high quality; this nuance is compressed.
Omits the key result that MIP increased fat mass versus protein-only (MD 0.76 kg, 95% CI 0.13 to 1.40) and the total body mass result.

'Pooling placebo and active controls can magnify the apparent blend effect' is the record's own inference. The source says the protein-only controls in the pooled comparison 'likely reduced the calculated effect size'.
The claim that protein supplementation may help meet rehabilitation nutrition targets goes beyond the source; the review included only healthy, non-injured adults.
Safety, third-party testing and cost guidance are generic and not drawn from the review; misses the authors' point that any MIP should contain substantial protein.

note: A reproduces every pooled estimate correctly, including the fat-mass increase versus protein-only and the dairy-funding disclosure; B is accurate on headline effects but omits the fat-mass finding and adds unsupported inferences.
